label: early copy phase, 3rd output (recall_idx 2) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during original input or at <DEL>. It is concentrated on the step that outputs the third original token (recall_idx 2, i.e. input = orig(1), two steps after <DEL>). That step holds 76% of activation mass, with weaker spillover at recall_idx 1 and 3 (~12% and ~11%) and essentially nothing later. Rate rises with sequence length: about 0 for L<=4, highest for L=9. All top activations (up to 4.5) are at recall_idx 2 in L>=7 sequences. Within that position, firing depends on token identity in a diffuse way: outputs h/u/j/i/2 and inputs 0/b/r are enriched, but no compact token set improves F1 (precision stays ~0.37). So precision is low (~0.22): most recall_idx-2 steps in long sequences stay silent. Never fires on first occurrences of a token (in_first=1 always inactive, which is trivially true in the copy phase), and never fires when copying has already gone wrong.
